newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 10-year bond flirts with 8.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 10-year bond flirts with 8.0 pct.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond yield flirted with the 8.0 percent barrier at one stage during afternoon trading as the market braced for the U.S. PPI later on Friday
*Futures roll-over takes up a large proportion of turnover.
The Australian 10-year bond yield flirted with the 8.0 percent barrier at one stage during afternoon trading as the market came under intense pressure ahead of the U.S. PPI later on Friday.
"The market has been weakening all day, and although 8.0 percent is the ceiling for now, it really is down to the PPI about where we go from here," one trader said.

A sharp sell-off in U.S. Treasuries following stronger than expected retail sales data put the skids under the local market from the opening, and if there is any sign of inflation pressures in the U.S. the market could be in for a rough ride.

In almost a re-run of last Friday's action ahead of U.S. non-farm payroll report, the markets are fearing the worst, but in the event, the markets rallied on detail contained within jobs report rather than the strong headline figures.
However, this time round while a benign PPI reading is expected, the report will be heavily scrutinised for any potential inflation threat, anaylsts said.
The headline PPI is expected to fall 0.1 percent, according to a Reuter survey of economists.
Traders added that a large proportion of today's trade was linked to roll over in futures ahead of Monday's March expiries.
The local sell-off saw yield differentials widen sharply to the U.S. and Canada and the 10-year spread to the U.S. backing up to the highs seen earlier this week.
